answer: The strongest lever is simple: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because grove only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, shale is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
